correctness.rationale: The source itself defines \(\digamma(T,\overline T)=rT-c^{-1}\int_{\overline T}^{T}q(t)\,dt\). Setting this equal to zero yields \(\int_{\overline T^*}^{T}q=crT\) exactly, which forces the missing factor \(T\) in the average-value closed-season formula and the missing factor \(1/c\) in the fixed-season growth-rate formula. The local-stability lower bound repairs to \((1/c)\int_{\overline T^*}^{\overline T}q\), preserving its sign. For the exact witness \(T=c=2\), \(r=1\), \(q\equiv4\), \(G=l=1\), \(E\equiv2\), the true root is \(1\), the printed root is \(1/2\), and at \(\overline T=3/4\) the per-cycle logarithmic growth is at most \(-1/2\), proving global extinction. verify.py replays all arithmetic exactly.

value.rationale: These factors determine management cutoffs between extinction and persistence. The exact witness shows a qualitative reversal: the printed closed-season formula puts \(\overline T=3/4\) above threshold, while the actual dynamics contract by at least \(e^{-1/2}\) per cycle and go extinct. The repair is compact, exact, and directly useful to anyone applying the paper's fishery calibration; it is not merely a typographical normalization check.
